text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT created — elevated errors & latency on streaming responses (prod-us-west) detected at 09:12 UTC. Auto-alerting SRE rota and pushing initial diagnostics.

sre_maya: I'm on it. seeing spike in 95th latency for /v1/stream and a rise in chunk-send timeouts. non-stream endpoints look fine. current error rate ~7.8% for streaming frames.

runtime_dev_jon: logs show repeated `write timeout` from the muxer layer + backlog growth on the GPU workers. suspect continuous batching + large prefixes causing KV cache thrash.

eng_oncall: paging oncall (ops_lee) and runtime team. @ops_lee can you confirm capacity / network egress for the cluster?

ops_lee: checking. network looks ok. some hosts reporting long GC pauses on the inference shim (p95 CPU steal). I can reduce concurrency on the serving pool to relieve pressure temporarily.

sre_maya: plan suggestion: 1) flip streaming feature to fallback mode for non-critical customers (let streaming -> short-poll responses), 2) shift a fraction of traffic to dedicated capacity or to non-streaming endpoints, 3) apply rate-limiter adjustments for bursty clients.

pm_ana: need to know customer impact. which customers will see changes? can we exclude enterprise/Dedicated tiers?

sre_maya: yes — we can target the toggle to only affect hosted streaming on the public model route. Dedicated customers and pinned model versions unaffected. We'll keep enterprise on full streaming.

runtime_dev_jon: to flip we're using the runtime control plane flag — quick command:

```
# temporary: set public streaming to degraded mode
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/flags/streaming_degraded" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" \
  -d '{"enabled": true, "scope": "public-hosted", "reason": "mitigation: elevated streaming errors"}'
```

sre_maya: also we can adjust per-customer streaming concurrency via the rate limiter API to reduce retries and frame pressure. Example:

```
# lower concurrency for free-tier customer bucket
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/rate-limits" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" \
  -d '{"bucket": "free-tier", "stream_concurrency": 1, "burst": 2}'
```

eng_oncall: I'm going to coordinate the flip now. I'll announce a status update after change and watch metrics (latency, 5xx, token throughput) for 5m.

cs_harper: heads up — support stack: customers on the public-hosted API might see their streaming clients drop back to a polled/chunked response shape. I'm drafting a short post for Status and a canned response for CS.

pm_ana: keep enterprise customers off the toggle. we must notify any big customers if their SDKs will adjust behavior.

sre_maya: executed the control-plane change at 09:18 UTC. streaming_degraded enabled for scope=public-hosted. rolling config applied to edge nodes.

runtime_dev_jon: I'm seeing the mux queues shrink and a drop in `write timeout` logs within 30s. 5xx rate down to ~3.2% so far.

ops_lee: reduced serving concurrency by -25% on a subset of nodes as a second mitigation.

pagerduty-bot: @ops_lee acknowledged the page. Escalation policy paused.

eng_oncall: monitoring: 1m/5m/15m windows look stable. CPU steal decreased; network egress steady. However, token throughput dropped ~12% for public-hosted streaming ops — expected tradeoff.

cs_harper: Status page draft: "We are temporarily routing public-hosted streaming requests to degraded streaming mode to stabilize latency. If you rely on continuous streaming, we recommend switching to the dedicated offering or polling fallback for critical flows. We will post updates every 15 minutes." want review before post.

pm_ana: good. include note that Dedicated customers unaffected and that this is a mitigation, not a permanent change.

sre_maya: next steps: keep degraded mode for min 30m while we run a runtime patch to improve KV cache eviction in the muxer. If error rate stays <1% and latencies normalize, we'll re-enable full streaming with a controlled ramp (10% increments over 10m).

runtime_dev_jon: starting a canary build with a quicker KV eviction policy now. test job kicked off.

eng_oncall: also enabling additional telemetry on frame sizes and client idle timeouts so we can target the real hot paths.

cs_harper: posted status update at 09:27 UTC. link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2245000000 (internal draft). added canned responses for CS.

sre_maya: running a short customer impact sweep: listing top 10 customers by streaming qps and their current mode. so far 5 of top10 are enterprise/dedicated (untouched), 3 are power-tier (bumped to degraded but we sent notices), 2 are free-tier (now in degraded mode).

pm_ana: ok. notify legal if any SLA exposures needed.

ops_lee: patch for the GC/steal symptom is non-trivial; prefer to keep degraded streaming until the faster eviction can be validated in canary + staging.

runtime_dev_jon: canary passed unit tests and integration, rolling to ~5% of edge nodes now.

sre_maya: metrics: 5xx for streaming down to 1.1%. p95 latency improved by ~220ms vs pre-mitigation. will hold for observation window.

eng_oncall: timeline: flip at 09:18, observe improvement by 09:19, canary running at 09:29. next check-in in 15m.

cs_harper: support queue: some customers reporting SDK reconnect messages, but no data loss for majority — they see chunked final payloads.

pm_ana: prepare comms for customers who need immediate re-enable — we can temporarily whitelist by org-id if required.

sre_maya: added whitelist for orgs via admin API. example below:

```
# add org to streaming whitelist
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/whitelist" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" \
  -d '{"org_id": "org-12345", "feature": "streaming", "expire_at": "2026-03-15T10:30:00Z", "reason": "customer request: critical flow"}'
```

eng_oncall: rolling additional telemetry/alerts to watch re-enable safely.

sre_maya: decision log: keep public-hosted streaming in degraded mode for now, continue canary for eviction fix, ramp re-enable only after 30m stable window and green canary. If regression occurs, revert to degraded and consider partial rollout per region.

cs_harper: filing a post-incident customer-impact spreadsheet and tagging affected orgs. will attach to incident ticket.

runtime_dev_jon: leaving a note for post-mortem: investigate batching heuristics and prefix length distribution causing KV thrash; add better bounding to avoid entire muxer contention.

eng_oncall: thanks team. if anything spikes, re-open page. will reconvene at 09:45 UTC for final decision to re-enable or extend mitigation.
